records.subject: Concern over the healthcare services in Kerala due to series of ongoing strikes.
records.SM_Text:
Smt. Jebi Mather Hisham: Kerala, a State long celebrated for its exemplary healthcare system, is witnessing an unprecedented disruption in medical services. With nurses on strike in private hospitals and doctors protesting in government hospitals, the healthcare system is facing a severe standstill. Several private hospitals are affected, with thousands of nurses participating in protests demanding fair wages and humane working conditions. Surgeries are being postponed, admissions restricted, and patients are forced to move from hospital to hospital in search of care.? At the center of this crisis lies a shocking reality. The basic salary of many nurses in private hospitals has remained ₹20,000 per month since 2018. For eight long years, despite inflation, rising costs of living, and the extraordinary sacrifices made during the COVID-19 pandemic, these frontline healthcare workers have seen virtually no meaningful revision in their wages. If Kerala?s hospitals begin to fall silent because its nurses are unheard, the responsibility will not lie with the nurses but with the system that ignored them. I urge the Government to intervene and ensure a fair national framework for nurses? wages and their working conditions.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Demand for sustainable livelihood support for Kerala’s fishing community.
records.SM_Text:
Smt. Jebi Mather Hisham:

I draw attention of the Government to a critical issue concerning the welfare of fishermen in Kerala. The fishing community, which forms the backbone of our coastal economy, is facing escalating operational costs due to rising fuel prices. To safeguard their livelihoods and promote sustainable fishing practices, I urge the government to enhance the allocation of non-subsidized kerosene and LPG for the fishing sector in Kerala.? Along with increased access to non-subsidized kerosene, promoting solar-electric fishing boats will also be a significant initiative towards the welfare of fishermen community. This initiative is not only economically beneficial but also environmentally transformative. Solar-electric boats significantly reduce operational expenses. Reduced fuel expenditure enables fishermen to keep more of their income, while maintenance requirements are also considerably lower. From an environmental perspective, the transition to solar-electric boats will substantially reduce carbon emissions and noise pollution, thereby protecting our fragile coastal ecosystems. The adoption of green technologies will enhance operational efficiency by providing a reliable and sustainable energy source for fishing activities. I urge the Government to grant a special package for Kerala to promote green fishing. This may include increased access to non-subsidized kerosene, incentives for LPG usage, and financial and technical support for solar-electric boats, benefiting thousands of fishermen across the State.? By combining economic relief with environmental responsibility, we can ensure a more secure and sustainable future for our coastal communities. I request the government to take necessary action in the interest and betterment of the fishing community.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Need for environmental and forest clearances for the Attappady Irrigation project in Kerala.
records.SM_Text:
Smt. Jebi Mather Hisham:?? I rise to emphasize the urgent need to obtain environmental and forest clearances from the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change for the Attappady Irrigation Project in Kerala. This project was sanctioned under the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal Award and conclusively upheld by the Hon?ble Supreme Court in its judgment dated 16 February 2018. Under this settlement, Kerala was allocated 30 TMC of Cauvery water, including 6 TMC for the Bhavani basin, of which 2.87 TMC is specifically earmarked for Attappady. This allocation constitutes a settled legal right, not a discretionary or negotiable claim.??????????? Despite this legal finality, the project continues to face procedural delays. A scientific Environmental Impact Assessment is required for environmental clearance, which in turn necessitates the issuance of terms of reference by the Ministry. Notably, the Expert Appraisal Committee identified no technical or ecological impediments. However, the proposal was returned citing the need for inter-state clearance. I urge the Ministry for the prompt issuance of the Terms of Reference and statutory clearances, recognising Kerala?s legal mandate to utilise its allocated share from the Bhavani basin, which is essential to ensure justice and development for the drought-prone, predominantly tribal region of Attappady, while upholding environmental responsibility.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Demand for safety audit of NH 66 and compensation for the families of those who have lost their lives at the NH construction sites.
records.SM_Text:
Smt. Jebi Mather Hisham: I rise to bring to attention of Government the recent collapse of a section of NH 66 at Kottiyam in Kerala. The accident shows the flaws in the execution of the National Highway projects in the State. The sudden caving-in of the road left the vehicles, including a school bus, stranded on the service road. The stability of the reinforced earth wall has been in question since the Kooriyad incident, wherein the National Highway collapsed in a similar manner. The vulnerable terrain of these places, owing to the proximity of paddy fields, cannot afford the present earth filling method. Apart from this, unscientific construction practices such as insufficient side-drain systems, poorly designed retaining structures etc. are leading to recurrent incidents of NH collapses. The public has been repeatedly raising concerns about unfinished work, absence of basic safety protocols during construction etc. The glaring example of the same is the unscientific construction of Aroor?Thuravoor stretch of NH 66, where at least 42 people have lost their lives in road accidents along this stretch, the latest one being the death of a driver who was killed when a girder collapsed onto a pickup van. In this context, I urge the Government to conduct a comprehensive technical audit of NH-66 and mandate strict adherence to scientific engineering standards. I further urge to take necessary steps for the immediate disbursal of compensation to the families of those who have lost their lives at the NH construction sites.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Demand for measures to curb the escalating menace of stray dogs.
records.SM_Text:
Smt. Jebi Mather Hisham : I draw attention to the escalating menace of stray dogs in Kerala, which has reached alarming proportions. Recently, schools and Anganwadis in Kozhikode district of the State were compelled to declare holidays due to the threat posed by stray dogs, with children particularly vulnerable to attacks. Over the past five years, Kerala has witnessed a significant surge in stray dog-related incidents. In 2024 alone, 3,16,793 dog bite cases were reported, a stark increase from 1,60,483 cases in 2020. Tragically, 94 individuals succumbed to rabies between 2020 and 2024, with 26 deaths occurring in 2024. The situation is further aggravated by a severe shortage of rabies vaccines, depriving many victims of timely medical care. Despite the sterilization and vaccination programs, the stray dog population continues to grow.? Recognizing the crisis, the Supreme Court appointed the Justice (Retd.) Siri Jagan Committee to recommend compensation for victims. However, the implementation remains inconsistent and delayed. The State must safeguard human lives, and therefore, it must bear the full medical expenses of those affected. Moreover, the compensation recommended by the apex court must be strictly enforced. I strongly urge the Union Government to sanction a special package to help Kerala combat this crisis. Immediate and decisive measures are needed to protect our citizens, especially children, from this growing threat.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Demand for measures to safeguard the rights of employees in Corporate sector.
records.SM_Text:
Smt. Jebi Mather Hisham: I may bring to the attention of the House the untimely death of a 26-year-old Chartered Accountant, hailing from Kochi in Kerala. It is learnt that excessive workload adversely affected her health which led to this unfortunate incident. This unfortunate incident exposes the unhealthy and exploitative work culture in corporate sector. Moreover, job insecurity is created through threats of layoffs. In the backdrop of this unfortunate incident, I urge the Central Government to do the needful to fill the gaps in the existing provisions of labour laws so as to safeguard the rights of employees. Clear provisions must be incorporated in the labour laws to address the working hours of remote employees. I request the intervention of Government to ensure a safe working environment for the employees in the corporate sector where their mental and physical well-being is not sacrificed for the sake of productivity.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Measures to construct elevated highway between Pulinchodu and Aluva
records.SM_Text:
Smt. Jebi Mather Hisham: I may bring to the attention of this House, the urgent demand for an elevated Highway between Pulinchodu at Aluva and Kochi international airport at Nedumbassery along NH544 in Ernakulam district, Kerala. Kochi international airport is India?s one of the fastest growing airports with three terminals and has established itself as one of the busiest airport hubs of the world. The number of passengers who depend on the airport has witnessed an exponential rise over the years. The current road infrastructure is highly insufficient to handle the bustling traffic, comprising of airport bound passengers and daily commuters. In this context, it may be noted that almost all airports in the metropolitan cities and other major cities in the country have elevated highway access. NH 544 which is the major road leading to the airport, has several bottlenecks which literally strangle the vehicular traffic from Kochi city and back ? Aluva bypass junction, Marthanda Varma bridge, Paravur Kavala, Athani are some of the places which witness the worst gridlock. The absence of grade separators and effective signals at major junctions has created traffic bottlenecks. This stretch, not being a part of Panvel-Kanyakumari NH development project, seems to be not in the priority list of NHAI. The proposal for extension of Kochi Metro to the airport was a ray of hope for the commuters but it remain still on paper.? Hence, I urge the government to take immediate steps for the construction of an elevated Highway between Pulinchodu and Kochi international airport.

 

(Ends)

records.subject: Measures for the welfare of duck farmers
records.SM_Text:
Smt. Jebi Mather Hisham: I would like to draw the kind attention of the House to the distress faced by duck-rearing farmers in Kerala, who are continually losing their livelihoods due to the intermittent outbreaks of bird flu (avian influenza). The bird flu scare has resurfaced in Kerala, particularly in the Alappuzha district. Thousands of birds, predominantly ducks, have either died or been culled in recent years. Besides ducks, the infection can also affect hens, quail, geese, and other ornamental birds.The virus outbreaks have become an annual issue. Early confirmation of these outbreaks is crucial to limit culling to smaller areas and prevent massive economic losses for farmers. Farmers need proper scientific advice to manage such situations effectively. Regular monitoring of wild aquatic birds and the bird-poultry-wetland interface is essential to understanding the prevalence of avian influenza viruses. A year-round surveillance mechanism for migratory birds is also vital to understanding their role in spreading the virus. Simply banning duck-rearing for a period is not a sufficient measure to contain bird flu.Local communities are bearing the brunt of these outbreaks, facing substantial economic losses that undermine their livelihoods. I urge the government to take immediate action to establish a National Institute of High-Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD) in Alappuzha, similar to the one in Bhopal, to enable early detection and confirmation of the virus. Additionally, a special financial aid package should be granted to support farmers who have incurred significant losses.?

(Ends)

records.subject: Demand for central assistance for the revival of agricultural sector in the state of Kerala
records.SM_Text:
Smt. Jebi Mather Hisham: The State of Kerala is passing through a tough phase consequent to the heavy landslides at Wayanad that has devastated the lives of people. The extreme weather conditions are constantly creating havoc in the state.Agriculture is one among the major sectors which bears the brunt of climate change and the subsequent weather extremities. The severe drought in Kerala during the summer of 2024 is estimated to have caused direct crop damage to 23,700 hectares across the state and a loss of Rs 260 crore. Indirectly, there is a loss of production in 23,000 hectares and the loss is estimated at 250 crore rupees. More than half a lakh farmers have been affected by the drought. Farmers belonging to the major agricultural districts of Idukki, Wayanad, Palakkad and Thrissur have suffered significant losses. The harsh drought has resulted in partial or complete losses of both food and cash crops. It is learnt that Govt. of Kerala has approached the Central Government for additional funds to address the situation and support the affected farmers. In this context, I appeal to the Central Government to grant a special financial package for the revival of agricultural sector in the state. It is requested to issue directions to Banks to write off the agricultural loans of the farmers? whose crops have been destroyed. I further urge the Government to provide special financial assistance to the people of Wayanad for compensating the losses in agriculture and livestock.

 

(Ends)

records.subject: Need for introduction of separate pay scale and other service benefits to ASHA workers.
records.SM_Text:
Smt. Jebi Mather Hisham: ASHA workers who are the backbone of rural health infrastructure have been tirelessly striving to bridge the gap between communities and the healthcare system. ?A million champions of health and hope? ? is how our Hon?ble Health Minister had described them when they were honored with Global Health Leaders? Award by WHO in May 2022. However, their crucial role is often undervalued with meagre remuneration, lack of benefits, and challenging work conditions.

Their work is conveniently brought under the umbrella of social or voluntary service and are paid with scanty honorariums and incentives. ASHA workers are currently paid fixed honorariums, often amounting to just Rs. 6,000 per month. This is highly inadequate as far as their extensive workload and responsibilities are concerned.

No social security and lack of EPF, healthcare and pensions leaves them financially vulnerable. Immediate measures should be taken to clearly define their work and accordingly introduce a separate pay scale and other service benefits.

Investing in the welfare of ASHA workers is an investment in public health and social well-being. Ensuring a fair pay structure will definitely boost the morale of ASHA workers and encourage them to stay in the program leading to greater continuity and effectiveness of healthcare services.??

In this context, I urge the Central Government to appoint a high-level Commission to study the factual position and to make necessary recommendations for the betterment of ASHA workers.

(Ends)

records.subject: Demand for enhancement of salary and other service benefits of Anganwadi employees
records.SM_Text:
SHRIMATI JEBI MATHER HISHAM (Kerala): Sir, the Anganwadi workers and helpers who are shouldering the immense responsibility of catering to the nutritional and various other developmental needs of the children and also to the nutritional programmes for the adolescent girls and pregnant women, are now in distress. There is no hike in their salary for the past seven years. The present monthly salary of Anganwadi helpers is Rs. 12,000 and that of Anganwadi workers is Rs. 8,000 in Kerala. This should be enhanced to a minimum of Rs. 21,000. There should be a provision to bring about their salary revision along with that of Government employees. Even though subscription amount is being collected towards Anganwadi workers and helpers welfare fund, benefits are not enhanced in accordance with the amount collected.

Anganwadi employees are facing various difficulties in performing their duties on a daily basis. They are not given performance grant for the data collection work in respect of various programmes and projects implemented at various levels starting from the Panchayat level. Since all of them do not have smartphones, they find it practically difficult to upload this data. Every expense including the payment of electricity and water bills of the Anganwadi centres, travel expenses for attending official meetings, etc., have to be borne by them, which is burdening them even more.

In this context, I urge the Central Government to appoint a high-level Commission to study the factual position and to make necessary recommendations for the betterment of Anganwadi helpers and workers.

(Ends)

records.subject: Need to revamp football training facilities in the country
records.SM_Text:
Smt. Jebi Mather Hisham : The involvement of Indians in the meticulous management of various sectors connected with the organisation of FIFA World Cup 2022 has won us accolades. While this is a moment of pride for us, we also need to address the grim reality that international football arena is still a distant dream for us.

A major impediment in the progress of Indian football is the lack of football specific stadiums. In my home state Kerala craze and passion for football is immeasurable. More than 5 lakh children actively participate in football training programmes in Kerala. These kids are training in mud football pitches without any proper training facilities. I request Government to set up training facilities in all districts with the support of state Governments and private partnerships.

Catch them while young should be the motto in training. Identifying talented kids and providing them international exposure by sending them abroad for a 5 to 10 years exclusive coaching in reputed football academies will be a sure success formula in crafting the future footballers.

The FIFA President commented recently that they are interested to invest heavily to develop football in India. In this context, I request Government to discuss this matter with the AIFF and AFC officials and prepare a detailed roadmap to develop the game in the country. A Football Academy with state- of- the- art training facilities should be given emphasis in the discussions. We should leave no stone unturned in ensuring our participation in the 2026 World Cup.

(Ends)

records.subject: Demand for inclusion of maximum number of people under National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP).
records.SM_Text:
SHRIMATI JEBI MATHER HISHAM (Kerala): Sir, I thank you for having given me the opportunity. It is the duty of the nation to ensure a dignified life for the deprived sections like the elderly and the widows in the context of higher cost of living. The Government should come forward to increase the central share of the pension scheme under the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP).

It is the need of the hour to take appropriate measures to restructure the current criteria for social security pensions under NSAP from household to individual indicators, instead of restricting the assistance to the beneficiaries in BPL families. It is essential to simplify the formalities to ensure that elderly persons with minor income would not be forbidden from the social security pension.

Instead of complete exclusion, the Government must have a better approach focusing on maximum inclusion of widows, elderly or disabled persons as found eligible, regardless of their family background. Such an approach could reduce dependence on their relatives.

Indias elderly population is projected to touch 194 million in 2031 from that of 138 million in 2021, according to the National Statistical Office Report, 2021. The prevalence of non-communicable diseases such as diabetes, hypertension, etc., is high among the elderly, the treatment cost of which turns out to be higher. The inverse relationship between poverty and higher out-of-pocket health expenditure should not go unattended.

At this juncture, I urge the Government to be kind enough to accommodate the maximum number of beneficiaries under NSAP. Thank you very much.

(Ends)

records.subject: Demand for provision of funds for the welfare and well-being of general public.
records.SM_Text:
SHRIMATI JEBI MATHER HISHAM (Kerala): Sir, this House was informed on 3rd August, 2022 that about Rs.10 lakh crore was written off in the last five financial years. If so, why don?t the Government waive off the loans given out to the small farmers under the Kisan Credit Card Scheme lending Rs.1.6 lakh credit without collateral? Having expected a positive turn in the economy, the Central Government has tried to give incentives to various players including the corporate. However, the motive is not seen fulfilled. Further, no concrete action plan has so far been devised to recover tax arrears, estimated at more than Rs.21 lakh crore. In such a context, the contention raised against offering freebies to ordinary people is not justifiable. While the big corporate leave the economy in peril, the well-being of the ordinary people and the downtrodden should not be side-lined. The people, who have been the pivotal stakeholder of our democratic system, are entitled to claim a reasonable "dividend" out of the Indian Parliamentary Democracy. And the welfare of the people needs to be the foremost priority of a democratic nation. I urge the Government to take necessary steps for the wellbeing of ordinary people.

(Ends)
